meta.name: The Baltic, 1906
meta.description: Northern Europe in 1906: Sweden and newly independent Norway, Denmark at the straits, the German Empire along the southern shore and the Russian Empire from Finland to Lithuania, around one inland sea.
meta.blurb: A real-world map: five realms, two empires and three small kingdoms, around the Baltic.
meta.style: Great powers and small kingdoms around one sea

nations.name: Kingdom of Sweden
nations.summary: A long kingdom of forest, ore and timber, newly parted from Norway, with a navy guarding the Baltic coast.
nations.strength: Iron ore and timber: industry starts cheaply.
nations.constraint: Long, thinly settled north: distances weigh on every campaign.

nations.name: Kingdom of Norway
nations.summary: Independent since 1905: a seafaring kingdom of fjords and mountains whose merchant fleet sails every sea.
nations.strength: Shipping: trade pays more, and straits cost less to cross.
nations.constraint: Mountains and few people: a small army.

nations.name: Kingdom of Denmark
nations.summary: A rich farming kingdom on its islands and Jutland, holding the straits between the Baltic and the North Sea.
nations.strength: Dairy and trade: income and influence above its size.
nations.constraint: Small and close to Germany: it must find friends.

nations.name: German Empire
nations.summary: The industrial empire of the north German plain, from the Ems to the Memel, building a fleet to rival any.
nations.strength: Industry and research: factories and schools ahead of every neighbour.
nations.constraint: Two seas and two fronts: every war is on more than one.

nations.name: Russian Empire
nations.summary: The empire’s north-western lands: the capital on the Neva, the Grand Duchy of Finland, the Baltic provinces, Lithuania and northern Poland.
nations.strength: Vast manpower: armies are cheap to fill.
nations.constraint: Restless borderlands: new provinces integrate slowly.
